summary: This note is a Wikipedia overview of Spain. It covers the country's location and territory, including its Mediterranean and Atlantic islands and its North African cities Ceuta and Melilla, and its borders, including the only European land border with Africa at Morocco. It also summarizes Spain's dominance of football and its national team's major tournament wins, and lists the country's public airports by passenger traffic, led by Madrid (Barajas) and Barcelona (El Prat).
one_line: Overview of Spain's geography, territories and borders, its football success, and its busiest airports.
key_facts: Spain is officially the Kingdom of Spain (Spanish: Reino de España), a sovereign state located on the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe.

Spain includes the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean Sea, the Canary Islands off the North African Atlantic coast, the cities Ceuta and Melilla on the North African mainland, and several small islands in the Alboran Sea near the Moroccan coast.
Spain is the only European country to have a border with an African country, Morocco.
Spain's African territory accounts for nearly 5% of its population, mostly in the Canary Islands but also in Ceuta and Melilla.
The Spanish mainland is bordered to the north and northeast by France, Andorra, and the Bay of Biscay, and to the west and northwest by Portugal and the Atlantic Ocean.
The mainland is bordered to the south and east by the Mediterranean Sea, except for a small land boundary with Gibraltar.
Varieties of football had been played in Spain as far back as Roman times, and sport in Spain has been dominated by football since the early 20th century.
Real Madrid C.F. and FC Barcelona are two of the most successful football clubs in the world.
Spain's national football team won the UEFA European Football Championship in 1964, 2008 and 2012.
Spain's national football team won the FIFA World Cup in 2010 and is the first team to ever win three back-to-back major international tournaments.
There are 47 public airports in Spain.
The airport of Madrid (Barajas) had 50 million passengers in 2011, the world's 15th busiest airport and the European Union's fourth busiest.
The airport of Barcelona (El Prat) had 35 million passengers in 2011, the world's 31st-busiest airport.
Other main airports are in Majorca (23 million passengers), Málaga (13 million), Las Palmas (Gran Canaria) (11 million) and Alicante (10 million).
More than 30 Spanish airports have fewer than 4 million passengers.
